When I explained that there was traffic and that it was only 10 minutes I said please you can’t send me home, I was told words to the effect of: “This is UK and I can send you home, now SIT and WAIT.” I experienced this as rude, aggressive and said in a racist tone. I felt I was being disrespected and discriminated against, especially as I was there with a small child.
I was then told to sit and wait, but after around 30 minutes another person informed me that the doctor/nurse would still not see us. I do not understand why I was told to wait if it had already been decided that we would not be seen.
This situation caused significant distress to me and my child, and delayed an important vaccination. I consider the receptionist’s behaviour and language unacceptable and not in line with NHS standards of respect and equality.
I would like this to be investigated under your NHS complaints procedure. Specifically, I would like:
1.	A clear explanation of why my child was refused the appointment for being 10 minutes late.
2.	An explanation of why we were asked to sit and wait when it appears the decision not to see us had already been made.
3.	Confirmation of what action will be taken regarding the receptionist’s behaviour and the discriminatory tone of the remark “this is UK I can send you home, now sit and wait”.
4.	Assurance that this will not happen again to us or to other patients, and information on any staff training or changes you will make.
